# Bloom Branding Packs

## Outcome
Confidently edit a branding pack and know exactly what makes the change show up in a real book, without guessing. Branding is data + CSS + assets that Bloom stamps onto a book's front/back matter at "bring up to date" time.

## Branding folder anatomy
Each pack is `src/content/branding/<Name>/`:
- **`branding.json`** — the data. A `presets` array; each entry sets a `data-book` value on the book's bloomDataDiv. Fields: `data-book`, `lang` (usually `"*"`), `content` (literal HTML/text), `condition` (`always` = always overwrite, `ifEmpty` = only fill if blank). A `"//"` key is a comment (ignored).
- **`branding.less`** — pack-specific *formatting*. Must `@import "../branding-base.less";`. Compiles to `branding.css`.
- **image assets** — `.png/.svg/.jpg` referenced by `branding.json` (logos, the made-with-bloom badge). These must physically live in the pack folder.
- **`summary.htm`** — human description; not used at runtime.

Division of labor (stated at top of `branding-base.less`): rules that *place* branding on an xmatter page go in `bloom-xmatter-common.less` / the xmatter's `.less`; rules that *format* branding go in `branding-base.less` or the pack's `branding.less`.

### Common `data-book` branding slots
Set via `branding.json` presets; rendered by mixins in `src/content/templates/xMatter/bloom-xmatter-mixins.pug`:
- `xmatter` — **selects the xmatter pack** the branding uses (e.g. `"MXBScripture"` → MXBScripture-XMatter). This is how a branding picks its front/back matter.
- `outside-back-cover-branding-bottom-html` — the back-cover badge (the "Made with Bloom" / QR badge).
- `title-page-branding-bottom-html` — logo at the bottom of the title page.
- `cover-branding-top-html`, `cover-branding-bottom-html`, `credits-page-branding-bottom-html`, `inside-back-cover-branding-top-html`, etc.
- non-branding presets too: `copyright`, `licenseUrl`, `funding`, …

## The "Made with Bloom" badge and QR code
This is the most common branding task and has real gotchas.

- **Modern markup** (use this — it's QR-capable), as in `Default/branding.json`:
  ```html
  <div class='bloom-branding-wrapper'><a href='https://bloomlibrary.org/'><img class='branding' src='made-with-bloom-badge-text.svg'/></a></div>
  ```
- **Old markup** (no QR): `<img class='branding' src='Made with Bloom.png'/>`. A branding using this gets **no QR code**, because the QR feature only acts on the wrapper structure.
- **QR injection** happens at runtime in `BookStorage.UpdateQrCode` (called from `UpdateSupportFiles`): it finds `div.bloom-branding-wrapper > a > img.branding`, and **if the collection setting `ShowBlorgLanguageQrCode` is on**, appends `<img class='bloom-qrcode' src='lang-qr-code.png'>` (generated by the `QRCoder` package, links to `bloomlibrary.org/language:<langCode>`) plus a `.bloom-lang-on-blorg` label, and rewrites the `<a href>` to the language URL. If the setting is off, it strips the QR img/label and removes the href — the badge still shows, just without a QR.
- **Badge SVGs** live in branding folders: `made-with-bloom-badge-text.svg` (with "Made with Bloom" text — what Default uses), `made-with-bloom-badge.svg`, and dark/white variants elsewhere. To use one, copy it into the pack folder (it gets copied into the book; relative `src`).
- **Sizing** comes from `branding-base.less` `.bloom-branding-wrapper`: white box, red border, `img.branding` width `4.7cm`, `.bloom-qrcode` width `2.8cm`, label `max-width 7cm`.
- **GOTCHA:** a pack-level override like `[data-book="outside-back-cover-branding-bottom-html"] img { width: 50% !important }` will hit *both* the badge and the QR images and break the wrapper layout. Remove such overrides when switching a pack to the wrapper/QR markup.

## How a branding change actually reaches a book (READ THIS)
A source edit does **not** show up in a running Bloom until two things happen:

1. **Build/deploy:** the content build copies `src/content/branding/<Name>/` → `output/browser/branding/<Name>/` and compiles `branding.less` → `branding.css`. A bare LESS `--watch` may recompile `.css` but does **not** necessarily copy new `.json`/`.svg` assets. After adding a new asset (e.g. a badge SVG), make sure the content build ran so the file exists under `output/browser/branding/<Name>/`.
2. **Book re-stamp (reopen):** when a book is opened / brought up to date, `BookStorage.UpdateSupportFiles` runs `LoadCurrentBrandingFilesIntoBookFolder()`, which copies **every** `.png/.svg/.jpg/.css` from the resolved branding folder (`BloomFileLocator.GetBrandingFolder(BrandingKey)`, i.e. the `output` copy) **into the book folder**, applies the `branding.json` presets to the data-div, and runs `UpdateQrCode`.

**Classic failure:** the book's DOM shows the new badge markup (references `made-with-bloom-badge-text.svg` / `lang-qr-code.png`) but the page shows "image missing." That means the book was partially re-stamped but the files weren't copied — almost always because the branding wasn't deployed to `output` yet, or the book hasn't been reopened since. Fix: rebuild content, then **close/reopen the book (or restart Bloom)** so `UpdateSupportFiles` copies the assets and generates `lang-qr-code.png`.

So the reliable loop for branding work: **edit source → content build → reopen the book in this worktree's Bloom.**

## Verifying changes

### In real Bloom (authoritative) — target THIS worktree's instance
Other agents run Blooms from other worktrees on other ports. **Never trust a bare CDP/HTTP port.** Use the `bloom-automation` skill:
- `node .github/skills/bloom-automation/bloomProcessStatus.mjs --json` — reports each Bloom's repo root; confirm one matches this worktree.
- Launch this worktree's Bloom with `./go.sh` if needed; take the HTTP port from its `Bloom ready.` line.
- `node .github/skills/bloom-automation/webview2Targets.mjs --http-port <port> --json --wait` — get the correct CDP target for *that* instance.
- On the Edit tab, the book page is in the iframe named `page`; the page list is `pageList`. Switch size via the `editView/topBar/layoutChoiceChange` API (`{layoutChoiceId}`) and select a page via `editView/jumpToPage` (POST body = pageId).

The runtime-only things (branding file copy into the book, real QR generation, autofit) **only** exist in real Bloom — so badge/QR work must ultimately be verified there, not in a static preview.

### Surveying many brandings at once — the branding viewer
When the question is comparative ("does this look right across every branding", "show me every
branding's back cover", "compare a branding across layouts"), don't drive Bloom by hand. Use
**https://github.com/BloomBooks/branding-viewer**, a standalone tool that walks
branding × page × layout × xmatter and screenshots each cell into a filterable web UI. It lives in
its own repo so a tester with only a CI-built Bloom can run it; nothing about it needs this
checkout.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/BloomBooks/branding-viewer   # once; needs bun, plus Chrome or Edge
cd branding-viewer
bun control.mjs                                  # interactive panel -> http://localhost:8798/
bun survey.mjs --brandings all --pages back      # batch capture
bun serve.mjs branding-viewer-out                # read-only viewer  -> http://localhost:8799/
```

Three things to get right:

- **`./go.sh` does not pass `--e2e`,** and without it Bloom does not register the endpoints the
  tool needs, so it refuses to start. Launch the exe directly instead:
  `./output/Debug/AnyCPU/Bloom.exe "<some.bloomCollection>" --e2e --automation`. The flag is a
  runtime check rather than `#if DEBUG`, which is what lets the same tool drive a Release build.
- **Point it at a *copy* of a collection.** It changes the collection's branding and the selected
  book's layout, restoring them on Ctrl-C but not on a hard kill.
  `src/BloomVisualRegressionTests/collections/basic` is a good throwaway, and it has both an A5
  Portrait and a 16x9 Landscape book.
- **Match the layout to the question.** Device16x9**Portrait** proves nothing about
  Device16x9**Landscape**; back-cover overflow only shows on short pages. And check which Bloom
  answered: the tool talks to whatever is on port 8089, often another worktree's instance. Its
  `manifest.json` records the `bloomVersion` it captured against.

The host half of the contract is `GET api/e2e/surveyOptions` and `POST api/e2e/setState` in
`src/BloomExe/web/controllers/E2eTestingApi.cs`. Change either shape in both repos together.

### Quick CSS preview without launching Bloom (non-authoritative)
Bloom books are self-contained (they carry their own `basePage.css`, `branding.css`, xmatter css, and the branding images). You can render the saved book `.htm` (or its xmatter pages) in headless Chromium with the book's own stylesheets plus a candidate-override CSS to iterate on *formatting* fast. Page dimensions come from the size class (`--page-width`/`--page-height` in `basePage.css`); swap the size class to preview other layouts. Headless screenshot needs `--virtual-time-budget=<ms>` or it shoots blank. **Caveat:** this uses the book's *already-stamped* css/markup and cannot run Bloom's runtime — it will NOT show the real QR, real branding-file copy, or prove the deploy. Use it for CSS layout iteration only; confirm the final result in real Bloom.

## Page sizes available to a branding's books
A branding's books get their page-size choices from the xmatter pack it selects. The dropdown is built from the **first** stylesheet containing a `STARTLAYOUTS … ENDLAYOUTS` JSON comment (parsed in `src/BloomExe/Book/SizeAndOrientation.cs`). That block lives in the xmatter `.less` (LESS preserves `/* */` comments into the compiled `.css`). For MXB this is in `MXBLiteracy-XMatter.less` / `MXBScripture-XMatter.less`. Note: although a code comment claims a branding-induced xmatter only sets a *default*, in practice that block *restricts* the available sizes.

## Key source files
- `src/content/branding/branding-base.less` — shared branding formatting incl. `.bloom-branding-wrapper`, `[data-book*="branding"]`, orientation helpers.
- `src/content/branding/<Name>/branding.json` / `branding.less` — per-pack data + formatting.
- `src/content/templates/xMatter/bloom-xmatter-mixins.pug` — the mixins that emit the `data-book="*-branding-*-html"` slots.
- `src/BloomExe/Book/BookStorage.cs` — `UpdateSupportFiles`, `LoadCurrentBrandingFilesIntoBookFolder` (copies branding files into the book), `UpdateQrCode` (QR/badge logic).
- `src/BloomExe/web/controllers/BrandingSettings.cs` — branding folder/file resolution.
- `src/BloomExe/Book/SizeAndOrientation.cs` — `STARTLAYOUTS` page-size parsing.

## Gotchas checklist
- Added a new asset but it shows "missing" → it wasn't deployed to `output/browser/branding/<Name>/`, or the book wasn't reopened.
- QR not showing → either the pack still uses the old `<img>` (non-wrapper) markup, or the collection's `ShowBlorgLanguageQrCode` setting is off.
- Badge/QR mis-sized → a pack `branding.less` `[data-book=...] img { width: … }` override is fighting `.bloom-branding-wrapper`. Remove it.
- Editing `branding.json`/assets but seeing no change → you only recompiled LESS; you also need the content build + a book reopen.
- Driving "Bloom" gives confusing results → you're attached to another worktree's Bloom. Verify repo root with `bloomProcessStatus.mjs --json`.
- The three MXB book brandings (`MXB-Book-Scripture`, `MXB-Book-Literacy`, `MXB-Book-Literacy-Prepub`) are edited together; Literacy and Literacy-Prepub share the same back-cover badge config.
